note: Rows a person has read. Each names the page or equation the claim comes from, and each `publishes` field is what that paper actually prints -- not what it could in principle be asked for. A paper absent from this list has not been read, and the census says so rather than leaving a blank that reads as a no.
read_by: Carles Marin, with Claude (Anthropic) as AI assistant

rows.label: Komori-Maru, SU(7) grand gauge-Higgs unification
rows.where: their Table 1: five contents, each with alpha_min, m_h and 1/R
rows.verdict: the anchor residue lives here. Our alpha runs 1.03x to 2.08x theirs across the five rows; a constant factor would be a convention, a varying one cannot be. It is why every absolute number in this instrument is labelled `measured`.

rows.label: Akamatsu-Hirose-Maru-Nago, two Higgs doublets from 6D
rows.where: minimum (0.438, 0.299); eq. (4.3) for M_W; eq. (4.4) gives 1/R = 303 GeV
rows.verdict: the one row in the corpus that our engine reproduces end to end: it lands on their published minimum at (0.437792, 0.298859), their ratio 1.2046 comes out 1.2045, and their own chain returns v = 246.0 GeV and 1/R = 303.0 GeV.

rows.label: Akamatsu-Hirose-Maru-Nago, the same model with brane kinetic terms
rows.where: minimum (0.438, 0.299) at c = 0 on p. 16 and (0.46, 0.30) at c = 15 in the caption of Fig. 1; eq. (5.19); the scale on p. 22
rows.verdict: their eq. (5.19) at their own c = 15 minimum gives 1171 GeV. The 1.4 TeV they print is that same equation with alpha_2 dropped (1398 GeV, four significant figures). Nine gates, including the one that could have failed: the same formula at c = 0 with their 2023 minimum returns their own published 303 GeV.

rows.label: Haba-Yamashita, the general 5D SU(N) formula
rows.where: sections 3 and 4 work four models in full, but their section 11 calls analysing the vacuum structure the hard part and leaves it
rows.verdict: the machine every model in this corner is built on, and it publishes no minima at all -- which is why the instrument's SU(N) builder is a builder rather than a table. All seventeen of its explicitly printed potentials are reproduced from section 5 alone.

rows.label: Haba-Hosotani-Kawamura, equivalence classes on S^1/Z_2
rows.where: the classification and its energetics, eq. (3.27); no phenomenological table
rows.verdict: formal. Its C(N+3,3) conditions, (N-1)N(N+1)/6 relations and (N+1)^2 classes are reproduced here at every N up to 14 as a property of the orbits walked, not as a quoted theorem.

rows.label: Takeuchi-Inagaki, a new classification of equivalence classes
rows.where: trace conservation laws, which their own text calls powerful NECESSARY conditions
rows.verdict: formal. On S^1/Z_2 the traces name the class; on T^2/Z_2 up to four classes share a triple and on T^2/Z_3 up to seven, measured here. Their own word is `necessary`, and it is the right one.

rows.label: von Gersdorff-Irges-Quiros, bulk and brane radiative effects
rows.where: critical N_f and the vacuum structure; no Higgs mass and no compactification scale
rows.verdict: one of the two anchor routes that are in print, and live in the instrument. Its four critical N_f are recomputed exactly. One discrepancy is declared and NOT resolved: our SU(3) value is 1/3 exactly on the Z_3 centre against their printed 0.29.

rows.label: Kojima-Kubo-Kubota-Yamashita and successors, the 6D construction
rows.where: eqs. (5.12)-(5.17), the quartet charge multisets per representation
rows.verdict: formal. Used here as a source of representation data, not of a phenomenological row.
